roles.label: Jackal
roles.summary: Irish man; conversational, wry, suddenly sharp when it matters.
roles.description: Native Irish English, a natural western Irish dialect. Male, 30 to 38. Excellent clean recording quality. Persona: dry-humoured infantry professional. Emotion: alert, wry, dependable. A medium-register masculine voice with a light sandpaper edge and easy conversational rhythm. Understatement and small changes in pitch carry the humour; the smile is audible without turning into a laugh. The instant someone is in danger, he becomes quick, clipped and forceful. Human uneven phrasing and brief breaths, casual confidence earned through experience. Lively spoken character dialogue at a brisk natural pace.

roles.label: Relay
roles.summary: Young North American woman; precise reports fraying under pressure.
roles.description: Native North American English, a clear general American dialect. Female, 24 to 30. Excellent clean recording quality. Persona: meticulous junior infantry leader. Emotion: attentive, determined, tightly wound. A bright middle-register feminine voice with precise consonants and quick thoughtful phrasing. She begins formally, choosing each word carefully. Under pressure her pace accelerates, her breath shortens and a small self-correction slips out, but her words remain intelligible. Earnest rather than theatrical; a human catch in the voice beneath practiced procedure. Capable of a sudden forceful warning, then consciously slowing herself back down. Natural spoken character dialogue.

roles.label: Ox
roles.summary: Older New Zealand man; warm bass and stubborn reassurance.
roles.description: Native New Zealand English, an unmistakably natural New Zealand dialect. Male, 50 to 60. Excellent clean recording quality. Persona: reassuring veteran infantry leader. Emotion: patient, grounded, stubbornly hopeful. A deep warm masculine bass with rounded resonance and a soft worn grain. Unhurried compact conversational phrasing, gentle downward inflection and an occasional smile in the voice. He speaks to his soldiers like people he knows and intends to bring home. Danger brings firm chest-supported projection and shorter phrases; anger carries disappointed gravity rather than a bark. Natural, expressive character dialogue with warmth still audible under exertion.

sections.text: Command, Ox. We are ready. Take your time. We will be here.
Contact. Easy, lads. Pick your shots. We are still here.
Friendly fire! Those are our people! Watch your aim!
Time to go. Back together, now. Nobody gets left on their own.
Still with you, Command. One thing at a time.

roles.label: Rivet
roles.summary: Older Lancashire woman; smoky, practical, dry irritation.
roles.description: Native British English, a grounded Lancashire dialect from north-west England. Female, 42 to 50. Excellent clean recording quality. Persona: practical infantry veteran. Emotion: sharp, irreverent, determined. A low-middle feminine voice with a smoky grain and occasional creak at the ends of phrases. Brisk economical speech and dry descending inflections. She treats danger like difficult work she knows how to do, reserving her irritation for avoidable mistakes. Practical warmth emerges through blunt encouragement. Her warnings cut through with firm rasp-edged projection, then settle immediately back into conversational speech. Natural character dialogue, older and heavier in timbre with minimal habitual shouting.

sections.text: Command, Rivet. Ready. Let us get this done before something else breaks.
Contact! Heads down. Use the cover.
Those are friendly rounds. Sort your bloody aim out.
Back, now. Bring your people. We are not dying here.
Still working, Command. You will hear when that changes.
